raw_recipe.headline: Apple Cider Chicken Marinade
raw_recipe.description: Marinate chicken in this recipe featuring white wine, apple cider vinegar, and an assortment of fresh herbs to help get moist chicken with a nice tangy flavor.
raw_recipe.name: Apple Cider Chicken Marinade

recipeInstructions.text: Whisk together the white wine, olive oil, lemon juice, cider vinegar, basil, parsley, rosemary, thyme, garlic, pepper, and salt in a bowl. Marinade chicken in mixture 8 hours or overnight.

review.reviewBody: Fabulous chicken marinade! I used this on boneless skinless chicken breasts (about 4) and I followed the recipe exactly. I poked the chicken with fork, put every thing into a ziploc bag and let it marinate overnight (which I highly suggest). I grilled it with a fresh sprig of rosemary and WOW -it came out so moist, juicy and full of the delicate flavor from the fresh herbs. It's a definite keeper. I served this with a side dish of "Bow Tie Pasta with Broccoli, Garlic and Lemon" from this site. Thanks for a great recipe, JustDMarine!

You guys! This marinade was so loved at my extended family gathering. All of the eaters were raving about the usual boring skinless boneless chicken breasts. Thankfully I was able to use fresh parsley and basil. The rest of the spices came from my spice rack. I doubled the batch for 8 breasts which I cut in half. There was about half a cup of marinade left after placing them on the BBQ grill. Also, I marinated them overnight and all day, about 20 hours thanks to some prior comments my preparation. The apple cider vinegar I used was the one with the mother, and also fresh lemon juice. The wine was a Sauvignon blanc, and not an expensive one. I served the chicken with sautéed fresh veggies and and a rice that I created, using a name brand box of rice pilaf and 2 packets of yellow rice, that has 2.5 servings. I added the right amount of water and butter and olive oil. It turned out great and wasn't too salty or dry. Thank you Debbie for posting this recipe!!

Terrific marinade! After marinading my chicken legs, I reduced the marinade almost to a glaze, while the legs were cooking. When the legs were almost done, I drizzled the marinade over them and put them back in the oven for 10 minutes.

I didn't have white wine or fresh herbs on hand, so I modified it a little and it turned out amazing! I used (for 6 servings):

1/2 cup extra-virgin olive oil,
1/4 cup fresh lemon juice,
3 tablespoons apple cider vinegar,
1 teaspoon dried basil,
1 teaspoon dried parsley,
1/8 teaspoon dried rosemary,
1/8 teaspoon dried thyme ,
3 cloves garlic minced,
1-1/2 teaspoons fresh-ground black pepper,
3/4 teaspoon salt.

I would use this marinade over a soy sauce marinade any day, and it's way healthier!
This is a great marinade. I love it just the way it's written as well as with 2 tbsp's soy sauce and 1 tbsp brown sugar. I usually use dry herbs because that's what I have on hand. Wonderful!

I had a similar chicken at the restaurant so I wanted to replicate. I get the marinade exactly as directed. I put it on the test and bun With melted brie cheese. I topped it with arugula and I had saved a little bit of the Marinade for a few dribbles on the arugula and added toasted walnuts it was fabulous. Thank you for the great recipe

Very nice marinade for chicken, could very well use for pork also. Ingredients were all on hand with the exception of some of the herbs. Had to use dried rosemary and thyme. Used boneless skinless breast. I let it marinade for about 6 hours, grilled them on the bbq and it was delicious. With the leftovers I'm going to have a very nice chicken salad for lunch!
easy to make and felt healthy with addition of ACV instead of soy sauce. used dried herbs instead (1 tsp instead of 1 tb) and minced garlice (1 tsp). smelled awesome and tastes great.

I grilled it. The entire family thought it was one of the best grilled chickens ever! I was worried because the marinade itself does not taste good. It's very bitter but the more the marinade sits with the chicken the more the tastes blend into something great!

I had a dinner party and got two amazing comments regarding this marinade "That was the best chicken I've ever had" and "That was better than any chicken I've ever eaten in a restaurant". Talk about rave reviews! It was the best chicken I've ever made. I used boneless skinless chicken breasts and marinaded them for 24 hours, rotating the chicken in the bowl after 12 hours. The only change I made was to double the fresh parsley in place of the basil.

I was looking for a new marinade for "beer can chicken," which is my favorite way to cook chicken. Used dried herbs instead of fresh and reserved marinade for basting. This was very easy, kid friendly, and good for a weekday meal.
I made this for boneless/skinless breast and bone/skin on thighs and they came out great. love the citrus flavor

I believe would enjoyed more if had been able to grill the chicken after marinading for 24+ hours. Trying new recipes while encouraged to stay at home during the coronavirus outbreak. I baked in the oven.

Used dried herbs because that is what I had on hand. Otherwise followed the recipe exactly. Marinated overnight and then grilled the chicken. The whole family loved it, even my kids who can be picky eaters!!! Thank you for the great recipe!!
came out great! kids and adults both loved it!
This recipe did not come out great for me. The vinegar was overpowering and the chicken tasted very bland even after marinating it for 24 hours. Maybe next time.

Not crazy bout this one. It made the chicken to fruity/acidic tasting. I cooked the chicken on a pan with olive oil. My opinion, if you use this recipe, cook on a grill and not in the kithen! The chicken was very juicy though, which was good!
This is really good! I added a little honey and left out the rosemary! The chicken was very moist. Thanks!
Cooked per recipe verbatim and, to the point, fantastic meal. I look forward to making this marinade again. Cut it up after grilling and used in a salad. This is on my top 5 chicken marinades!
Delicious marinade. Good use of fresh herbs from the garden.
